claim.pdf_says: DELETE Format 1 (record), 14.9.10.2. The INVALID KEY block is printed as ONE tall square bracket spanning both alternatives with a full-height vertical choice-indicator bar immediately inside each bracket:  [ |  INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 / NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2  | ] .
claim.markdown_says:
```
DELETE file-name-1  RECORD
  [ retry-phrase ]
  ⌐ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1     ¬
  | NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 |
  [ END-DELETE ]
```
claim.why_it_matters: The two inner choice-indicator bars (5.2.6.4) are gone: the markdown has exactly one glyph per side per row, so the four printed vertical strokes per row collapse to one. Without the bars the bracket reads as 'at most one of the enclosed alternatives', which would forbid writing INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY on the same DELETE statement. The standard permits both (14.9.10.4 GR 11 explicitly discusses 'the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases'), so the loss is toward falsely-restrictive syntax.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct pixel measurement of the rendered page, not by eyeballing. Page alignment first: PDF page 635 (printed footer 605) is 14.9.10 DELETE statement, and the markdown anchor at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:26305 opens the same 14.9.10 DELETE section, so the two sources are compared at the same page. (The TOC lines that point '14.9.19 IF statement' at #page-635 are a separate pre-existing TOC-anchor defect and do not affect this comparison.) PDF EVIDENCE: a column-ink profile over the Format 1 figure band (y=1110..1300 of the 2550x3300 300dpi render) finds exactly FOUR tall vertical strokes, not two: x=370-371 height 133px spanning y=1140..1272 with 18px of horizontal ink on its top and bottom rows (serif arms -> a '[' bracket); x=391-392 height 156px spanning y=1125..1280 with only 2px of ink on its top and bottom rows (no arms -> a bare vertical bar); x=1271-1272 identical bare bar; x=1293-1294 height 133px with 18px arms -> the ']' bracket. The inner bars are 23px TALLER than the bracket stems and carry no serifs, which rules out the refutation that this is one stretchy bracket rendered with a doubled stem. So the PDF genuinely prints [ | ... | ] exactly as claimed. MARKDOWN EVIDENCE: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:26324-26328 is verbatim what the claim quotes, and carries exactly one delimiter glyph per side per row ('⌐'/'¬' on row 1, '|'/'|' on row 2) -- the row-2 pipes are the transcription's bracket SIDES, not choice indicators, as proven by the corner glyphs occupying that same delimiter column on row 1. NO figure-note recovers the lost bars in prose; the page's md slice has none. NOT A CONVENTION: the transcription already has a correct 4-glyph rendering for this identical construct and uses it three times -- REWRITE (line 30096), START (line 31756) and WRITE (line 33001) all read '⎡ | INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 | ⎤ / ⎣ | NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 | ⎦', bracket corner PLUS a separate choice bar on each side. DELETE is the outlier that dropped them. SEMANTICS: 5.2.6.4 says choice indicators are 'a pair of bars, |,' and 'When enclosed by brackets, zero or more of the alternatives ... shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once', i.e. BOTH phrases are legal; 5.2.6.2 says a plain bracket admits 'the syntax element contained within the brackets or ONE of the alternatives', i.e. at most one. The transcription therefore states a strictly narrower syntax than the standard. The claim's supporting citation is accurate: 14.9.10.4 GR 11 (line 26411) reads 'Transfer of control ... depends on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the DELETE RECORD statement', which is incoherent unless both may co-occur. None of the rejection criteria apply: the glyphs are not present anywhere on the page, this is not reflow/page-break/hyphenation furniture, neither source is misquoted, and the meaning demonstrably changes. Direction of the error is toward falsely-restrictive syntax, matching the known OCR failure mode.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and the claim UNDER-states it: the defect hits BOTH figures on page 635, not just Format 1. Format 2 (file) has the identical loss -- the PDF prints four strokes there too (measured at x=370 h=145 with 18px arms, x=391 h=157 bare, x=1314 h=157 bare, x=1337 h=134 with 17px arms), i.e. '[ | ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 / NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 | ]', while specs/ISO_COBOL.md:32-33 of the page slice (file lines 26332-26333) again gives only '⌐ ... ¬' / '| ... |'. So DELETE FILE likewise reads as forbidding ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION together, when 5.2.6.4 permits both. Secondary precision fix: the markdown's row-2 '|' characters are the bracket sides, so the correct statement is not that 'four strokes collapse to one' in the sense of the bars surviving -- the two choice-indicator bars are deleted outright and the surviving glyph is the bracket. The fix for both figures is the transcription's own already-correct convention used at REWRITE/START/WRITE: '⎡ | ... | ⎤' over '⎣ | ... | ⎦'. Note also a related but distinct defect on another page, out of scope here but worth ledgering: READ (line 29483-29484) renders the same construct as '[ [ INVALID KEY ... ] ]', turning the choice bars into a second pair of brackets, which is also falsely restrictive.
